ct_el_duque_wall.blurb: El Duque Wall is a bouldering wall in the East Side section of the Bald Rock Basin in Connecticut. You reach it by working west across the hillside past the Welcome Wall. It is a tall face, roughly 18 to 25 feet, broken by cracks, crimps, pinches, slopers and some unusual intrusions, and it is regarded as one of the better walls in the basin. Ten problems climb it, running from V0 up to V5, with the biggest cluster around V3, so it suits a mixed group better than a pure project crowd. Bring a good set of pads and spotters, since the height makes the landings matter.

ct_clinton_road_boulder.blurb: Clinton Road Boulder is one lone block in the Quillinan Reservoir section of Naugatuck State Forest, on the Seymour and Ansonia line, roughly twenty minutes out of New Haven. It sits in a sunny spot a short way off the road, and the rock is good quality. Ten problems cover it, with a pair of easier V2 lines and one V3, but most of the problems are hard, in the V6 to V7 range, so it is mainly a stop for strong boulderers. The sun makes it a popular choice for cold-season sessions.

ct_emerald_city_slab.blurb: Emerald City Slab is a low-angle, lichen-tinted slab at Pinnacle Rock in central Connecticut, where the cliffs are basalt (traprock). The routes are short but fun, and a finger crack splits the slab down the middle. Of the ten climbs, most are trad with a few top-rope lines, running from 5.4 up to 5.10, with the bulk in the 5.7 to 5.8 range. Small cams and tiny TCUs handle the protection, and several lines are bold in places. Walking up the easy slab between here and the A-Frame Wall gets you to the top for setting up a top rope.

ct_upper_tier_2.blurb: The Upper Tier is the easier of the two cliffs at Wolf Rock in Mansfield, in Connecticut's eastern highlands. The cliff is short, about 30 to 40 feet, clean and sunny, and mostly slabby, with steeper cracks and sections toward the right. Ten climbs run from fourth class to 5.6, mostly trad with a top-rope line or two, and most are easy to lead or to set up on top rope with webbing. That makes it a good place for beginners and for teaching new climbers the basics.
ct_upper_tier_2.parking_note: Leave the car at a small pullout on Crane Hill Road.
ct_upper_tier_2.approach: Follow the blue-blazed Nipmuck Trail to a balanced boulder on top of the cliff, then descend to the right to reach the base.

ga_dug_mountain_hood_rock.blurb: Dug Mountain, also called Hood Rock, is a small bouldering area on a ridge near Dalton in northwest Georgia. The boulders are sandstone and mostly shaded, with a few good-quality blocks and others that need some cleaning. Nine of the ten climbs are boulder problems, spanning V2 to V6, with one harder 5.x trad line. Some problems are steep and tall enough that a good pad and spotters are worthwhile. Most of the boulders sit within a few minutes' walk of the top of the mountain, along a flat, gravel trail.

ga_white_wall.blurb: White Wall is a granite wall on Mount Yonah in northeast Georgia, the lowest of a scattered group of smaller walls below and to the right of the Lowers. The rock is high quality, with interesting holds, and most of the climbing is crimpy face work on slab. Ten routes mix sport and trad, with a few top-rope options, from 5.7 to 5.11. The sport lines are the popular draw and have bolted anchors, while the trad lines around them are dirtier and less visited, and finish at tree anchors. Expect a long uphill hike to reach it.

ga_iron_claw_area.blurb: Iron Claw Area is a cluster of sandstone boulders at Rocktown in northwest Georgia, sitting just above a stream and named for its best-known problem. Ten problems range from V3 to the V10 range, from approachable lines to some serious hard sits, so it favors strong boulderers. Because the blocks are close to the water, it is best visited after a dry spell: a sit start can be close to impossible after rain, though stacked logs over the stream usually keep stand starts accessible.
